facts.raw_span: 2-year history of multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
occasional slight pain extending from her left upper arm to the left side of her chest
No triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma occurred before lesion appearance
She denied fever, weight loss, or fatigue
Multiple firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders on her left axilla, medial upper arm, and lateral thoracic region
No extracutaneous involvement was observed
Thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels dispersed between thickened collagen bundles
Endothelial cells were plump but displayed no significant cytologic atypia
Positive for: CD31, CD34, Ki-67 (<1%)
Negative for: podoplanin (D2-40), human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)
Image A Description: Multiple nonscaly, erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques with irregular borders on the patient's left axilla, medial upper arm, and lateral thoracic region
Image B Description: Irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels dissecting through collagen bundles within the superficial to mid dermis
Image D Description: Endothelial cells positive for cluster of differentiation (CD) 31

concepts.why: The presence of thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels and positive immunohistochemistry results for CD31 and CD34 support this diagnosis

The clinical presentation of multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, along with the histopathological findings of thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels, support this diagnosis

rationales.F01: The patient's 2-year history of multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques is not typical of Kaposi's sarcoma or Angiosarcoma, but is more suggestive of Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma.
rationales.F07: The presence of thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels dispersed between thickened collagen bundles is more characteristic of Hemangioma or Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma than Kaposi's sarcoma or Angiosarcoma.
rationales.F08: The absence of significant cytologic atypia in the endothelial cells rules out Angiosarcoma and suggests a more benign condition such as Hemangioma or Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma.
rationales.F09: The positive staining for CD31, CD34, and Ki-67 (<1%) is consistent with Hemangioma or Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma, but not typical of Kaposi's sarcoma or Angiosarcoma.
rationales.F10: The negative staining for podoplanin (D2-40) and human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) rules out Kaposi's sarcoma and suggests a different diagnosis such as Hemangioma or Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma.
rationales.F12: The histopathological image showing irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels dissecting through collagen bundles is more characteristic of Hemangioma or Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma than Kaposi's sarcoma or Angiosarcoma.
